_comment: DEPTH AXIS. Fixed compute depth as the variable, for the compute-depth
scaling curve the research goal asks for.
Settings match the run that produced the reported first pass: per_cell 160,
indistinguishable 12, 600 steps, and AUTO-BATCH OFF with batch 6.
AUTO-BATCH IS DELIBERATELY OFF HERE. It is on for the data axes because it
gave 7.4x the throughput. The depth numbers were measured at fixed batch, so
switching it on would make this manifest no longer reproduce them — and a
depth comparison where the batch silently changed with the axis would confound
the axis.
Run:
cargo run --example scaling_sweep --
research/experiments/depth-axis.json depth gpu 1 2 4 8 --seeds=0,1,2
The sweep tool sets stop.fixed{loops} per point, zeroes ponder_weight (no
learned step count means the ponder term is a constant loss offset), and
raises max_loops to match. ACT is NOT on this axis.
READ WITH THE HALT PROFILE. Fixed depth and degenerate early halting look
identical in an accuracy table and are opposite claims. At high LR the stage
profile went to 5.2/1.6/1.0/1.0, which is degenerate early halting rather than
depth allocation. Report the per-stage profile next to any depth number.
KNOWN LIMITATION of the existing pass: exact-match was 0.000 on both halves at
every depth, so it only became legible once byte accuracy was added, and
within-seed spread exceeds every between-depth difference at n=3.
max_loops 8 here (not 4) so the axis can reach 8.
